title: Observability fallback circuit and customer escalation protocol
author: Mariana Liu
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This guide documents recommended integration patterns for Redwood customers to implement resilient telemetry and observability in the face of partial outages, plus the customer-facing escalation protocol that Support and Customer Success teams should follow when telemetry degrades or misreports. It covers: fallback circuit design, safe-mode telemetry striping, alert thresholds mapped to customer-facing severity levels, example Prometheus rules, sample incident payloads for downstream systems (PagerDuty / Zendesk), and a step-by-step escalation playbook for on-call and CSMs.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private customers and to hosted customers with custom telemetry forwarding.
- Focuses on metrics, traces, and request/response sampling paths handled by the telemetry-gatekeeper and ingress-gateway.
- Does NOT replace per-tenant security or compliance checklists; see the private deployment acceptance playbook for those gates.

Key concepts and terminology:
- telemetry-gatekeeper: our sidecar/proxy component that validates and forwards telemetry from tenant workloads to Redwood collectors.
- circuit: a set of fallback rules that switch telemetry routing when an upstream path fails (e.g., forward to local buffer, sample down, or switch to light-weight health pings).
- striping: sending a subset of telemetry (e.g., 10% of spans + aggregated metrics) to reduce load while preserving signal.
- safe-mode: temporary mode where we reduce cardinality, increase sampling, and rely on synthetic checks for customer-facing health.

Executive summary (1 paragraph):
When telemetry ingestion becomes unavailable or unstable, customers should automatically enter a controlled fallback that maintains core SLO observability: request success rates, latency p50/p95, and token rate. Implement telemetry circuits in the telemetry-gatekeeper: primary path -> durable buffer -> reduced-sample forwarders -> synthetic pings. Support and CSMs must run the escalation protocol below when customer-facing SLAs are impacted or telemetry misreports greater than 2x for 15 minutes.

Design patterns and recommended configurations

1) Fallback circuit topology (recommended ordering)
- Normal: telemetry-gatekeeper forwards to primary-hosted-collector (TLS, compressed).
- Failover 1 (transient): telemetry-gatekeeper switches to local-durable-buffer (disk-backed) and also mirrors a sampled stream (10% metrics, 1% traces) to secondary-collector.
- Failover 2 (sustained): telemetry-gatekeeper flips to safe-mode: metrics aggregated at 60s resolution, traces disabled, synthetic pings every 30s to tenant-monitoring-probe.
- Recovery: gated rollout back to Normal after sustained 30m of stable forwarding and synthetic success.

Implementation checklist (config snippets and thresholds)
- telemetry-gatekeeper config (yaml) example:

  apiVersion: telemetry.redwood/v1
  kind: GatekeeperConfig
  metadata:
    name: customer-telemetry-policy
  spec:
    primaryForwarder: https://collector.redwood.example/v1/ingest
    buffer: {"type":"disk","max_size_mb":512}
    safeMode:
      metric_resolution_seconds: 60
      trace_sampling_rate: 0.01
      synthetic_probe_interval_seconds: 30
    fallbackRules:
      - trigger: [["upstream_connect_errors", ">", 5, "1m"]]
        action: "mirror_to_secondary_and_buffer"

- Prometheus alert rules (critical examples):

  - alert: TelemetryPrimaryUnavailable
    expr: rate(upstream_connect_errors[1m]) > 5
    for: 1m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Primary telemetry collector connection error spike"

  - alert: TelemetrySampleRateDrop
    expr: telemetry_forwarded_samples_total / telemetry_received_samples_total < 0.5
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: major
    annotations:
      summary: "Effective telemetry sampling has dropped below 50%"

- SLO mapping table (example):
  | Customer SLA tier | Observability SLO maintained in fallback | Allowed data loss window | CSM notification level |
  | standard | request success rate p99 / 99% | 30m | Level 2 (notify) |
  | enterprise | request success rate p99 / 99.9% + latency p95 targets | 15m | Level 1 (paged) |

2) Telemetry striping recipes (to keep cardinality manageable)
- Metric cardinality cap: apply label whitelisting per tenant. Example policy: allow labels [route, status_code, model_family], drop others.
- Trace striping: use hash-based sampling: sample = hash(request_id) % 100 < N; recommended N=1-5 for safe-mode.
- Embedding/large-payload exclusion: do not forward raw embeddings; forward aggregated counts instead.

Operational thresholds and alerting matrix (customer-facing)
- Severity definitions for customer communications:
  - Sev 1 (P1) - Customer core inference is degraded or unavailable and no automatic fallback is possible. Action: page oncall SRE and CSM.
  - Sev 2 (P2) - Telemetry indicates degraded performance or misreporting that may materially affect incident response (e.g., sampling drop, metric staleness > 10m). Action: notify CSM and open a high-priority ticket.
  - Sev 3 (P3) - Non-urgent telemetry inconsistencies (dashboard gaps, minor metric divergence). Action: track in ticket queue; no page.

- Threshold examples (use as defaults; calibrate per customer):
  - Metric ingestion error rate > 2% sustained for 10m -> P2
  - Effective sample rate < 25% for 15m -> P2
  - Synthetic probe failure rate > 3 fails in 10m -> P1 if customer SLA is enterprise else P2

Escalation and customer communication protocol (step-by-step)

1) Detection and automatic mode switch (automated systems)
- Prometheus rule fires TelemetryPrimaryUnavailable -> alert routed to telemetry-team Slack channel and PagerDuty escalation policy "telemetry-forwarding".
- telemetry-gatekeeper automatically engages Failover 1 (buffer + mirror). An event is emitted to /events/telemetry/fallback with JSON payload (example below).

2) Triage by on-call SRE (within 10 minutes for P1 / 30 minutes for P2)
- Confirm the alert by checking collector health, network egress, and gatekeeper logs:
  - kubectl -n observability logs deploy/telemetry-gatekeeper --since=30m | grep "fallback"
  - curl -sS https://collector.redwood.example/health | jq .status
- Determine whether telemetry forwarding or customer traffic is impacted.
- If failover is successful and core customer traffic is unaffected, mark as "monitored" and notify CSM with templated status.

3) CSM outreach and customer notification templates (when to contact)
- Contact for P1 immediately after confirmation. P2 contact within 60 minutes.
- Use the following message template for CSMs (Slack/email/Zendesk):

  Subject: Redwood telemetry disruption for <tenant-name> — interim measures in place

  Hello <CustomerTeam>,

  We detected a transient issue impacting telemetry reporting for your deployment. We have automatically switched to a reduced telemetry mode to preserve application availability and are continuing to collect core metrics (request success rate, latency p50/p95). Our engineering team is investigating.

  Impact: reduced trace sampling and delayed metrics (up to 60s resolution)
  Expected next update: within 30 minutes
  Interim mitigations: safe-mode aggregation, synthetic probes enabled, buffering to durable storage

  If your team sees application-level errors or missing responses, please escalate to our oncall via PagerDuty (link) and include request IDs.

  Regards,
  Redwood Customer Success

4) Root cause analysis and recovery steps
- If the collector was the root cause: restore the collector, ensure TLS certs valid, and validate back-pressure counters are zero. Use these commands: 
  - kubectl -n observability rollout restart deploy/collector-primary
  - ssh collector-host && sudo journalctl -u collector -n 200
- If the gatekeeper buffer saturated: increase buffer size temporarily and force a replay from buffer once target collector reachable. 
- Recovery checklist (mark items in ticket):
  1. Confirm primary forwarder healthy for 30 consecutive minutes (no alert).
  2. Gradually reduce safe-mode sampling: 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> normal over 40 minutes.
  3. Rehydrate traces/metrics from buffer if required; check cardinality.
  4. Notify customer with final incident summary and link to RCAs.

Example event payload (emitted by telemetry-gatekeeper)

  {
    "event_type": "telemetry.fallback.engaged",
    "tenant_id": "tenant-1234",
    "timestamp": "2027-01-12T14:05:22Z",
    "fallback_stage": "mirror_to_secondary_and_buffer",
    "reason": "collector_connect_errors",
    "metrics_impact": "sample_rate_reduced_to_10%"
  }

Integration points with downstream systems
- PagerDuty: map Prometheus alerts: TelemetryPrimaryUnavailable -> PD escalation policy "infrastructure/telemetry". Include runbook link and event payload in PD notification.
- Zendesk: create ticket type "Telemetry Incident" and tag with tenant_id. Use send-to-customer template for P1/P2.
- QBR telemetry: automatically append incidents where a tenant entered safe-mode to the QBR summary feed; long-lived or repeated entries should trigger a stability review.

QBR & health-check signals to track
- Synthetic availability (30s probe pass rate) — target 99.9% enterprise, 99% standard.
- Number of safe-mode entries per quarter per tenant — target <=1 for enterprise.
- Mean time in safe-mode — target < 45 minutes.
- Percent of incidents where buffer replay caused data duplication — target 0%.

Testing and customer onboarding steps
- During onboarding, run the following simulation:
  1) Enable a controlled network block to the primary collector for 10 minutes.
  2) Verify gatekeeper enters Failover 1 and mirrors to secondary.
  3) Confirm telemetry sampling and synthetic probes continue to report.
  4) Restore network path and validate recovery checklist.
- Document results in the customer onboarding artifact and include telemetry circuit behavior in the cutover signoff.

Support playbook checklist (quick runbook for first responder)
1. Acknowledge alert and classify severity (P1/P2/P3).
2. Check collector health and gatekeeper logs.
3. Confirm fallback stage and whether core customer traffic is impacted.
4. Notify CSM with templated message.
5. If P1, page oncall SRE and open an incident ticket in the tracker.
6. Follow recovery checklist and update customer every 30 minutes until resolved.
7. After resolution, attach gatekeeper event payload and metrics to the incident and schedule RCA.

Ownership & contacts
- telemetry-runbook-owner: eng-platform-observability (pager: @telemetry-oncall)
- Customer Success escalation: cs-ops (email: cs-ops@redwood.example / pager: @cs-oncall)
- Escalation threshold arbiter: product-sre (for SLA disputes)

Appendix: useful commands and queries
- Check gatekeeper buffer stats (kubectl):
  kubectl -n observability exec deploy/telemetry-gatekeeper -- curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep buffer

- Prometheus query for sample-rate:
  rate(telemetry_forwarded_samples_total[5m]) / rate(telemetry_received_samples_total[5m])

- Example curl to replay buffer (operator-only):
  curl -X POST https://gatekeeper-admin.local/replay?tenant=tenant-1234 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>'

- Incident postmortem template link: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/incident-postmortem-template
